# Hermes Agent: Quick-Start & Troubleshooting FAQ

### 1. Installation & Environment Setup
- **Native Windows**: Windows 10/11 is Tier 1 supported via `install.ps1`. WSL2 is recommended if you need the embedded `/chat` terminal (requires a POSIX PTY).
- **Docker / ARM64 / NAS**: The official image `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` is multi-arch (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) supporting Raspberry Pi and Apple Silicon. For NAS volume permission issues (`[Errno 13] Permission denied` on `/opt/data/config.yaml`), pass `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`, e.g. `PUID=1000 PGID=10`).
- **Android (Termux)**: Supported out of the box; `install.sh` and `hermes update` use `.[termux-all]` and write temporary files to `$TMPDIR`.
- **Web UI Dashboard**: Run `hermes dashboard` to start the local web UI and browser chat at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`.
- **Diagnostics**: Run `hermes doctor` to verify your Python environment, virtualenv, dependencies, and authentication providers.
- **Update Stalls**: If `hermes update` pauses during the Node.js step, it is typically Camofox downloading browser binaries in the background.

---

### 2. Models & Provider Configuration
- **Local Models (Ollama / Qwen 4B–9B) Slow**: Hermes sends ~45 tool schemas per turn. Improve speed by disabling unused tools via `hermes tools`, using faster quantizations or larger models (32B+), and setting `terminal.backend: local` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
- **Local Endpoint Ignored (`base_url: http://localhost:11434`)**: If `provider: auto` picks up remote environment keys (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), set `provider: custom` and `fallback_providers: []` in `config.yaml`.
- **Ollama Cloud 404s**: Set provider to `ollama-cloud`; Hermes automatically targets `https://ollama.com/v1`.
- **Azure AI Foundry**: Set `provider: azure-foundry` and export `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` (run `hermes setup`). Claude Code-specific flags (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`) are ignored.
- **Gemini Auth**: Gemini CLI OAuth was removed due to upstream policy bans. Use Google AI Studio keys (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY`) or Vertex AI.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs API Credits**: Claude API keys are always billed per token by Anthropic. To use your Pro/Max subscription quota, authenticate via Claude OAuth.
- **Vision for Custom/Ollama Models**: Add `supports_vision: true` to your custom model configuration block.
- **Model Routing**: Hermes enforces session model consistency; automatic cost-based routing (`smart_model_routing`) is not supported. Switch manually via `/model` or `hermes chat -m <model>`, or configure subagents via `delegation.model`.
- **Token Usage / LocalAI**: Hermes sends `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` for OpenAI-compatible streaming and preserves provider-level `extra_body` configs.

---

### 3. Messaging Gateways & Personas
- **Interactive Setup**: Run `hermes gateway setup` to configure Discord, Telegram, and other channels without manually editing `.env`.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized user"**: `allowed_chats` is only a group response filter. To authorize DM access, add your numeric ID to `allow_from: "USER_ID"`, approve via `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`, or set `allow_all: true`.
- **Files & Media**: Gateways support inbound attachments (`.txt`, `.py`) and outbound file delivery (Matrix `m.file`, Email attachments, Telegram media, DingTalk Markdown `![image](url)`). Base64 MCP tool images tagged with `MEDIA:<path>` are forwarded automatically.
- **Open WebUI Streaming**: Real-time tool execution progress is streamed natively over SSE.
- **Personas & Profiles**: Set per-channel system prompts using `channel_prompts` in your platform config (Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost). To run multiple accounts, use profile-multiplexed gateways (`hermes gateway`) to keep sessions, memory, skills, and credentials isolated.
- **Multi-Agent**: Use `delegate_task` to spawn concurrent child `AIAgent` instances with isolated context.

---

### 4. Memory, Skills & Extensibility
- **Prompt & Profile Files**:
  - `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: Agent persona, character, and instructions.
  - `~/.hermes/USER.md`: User profile and identity (updated via memory tool `target="user"`).
  - `~/.hermes/MEMORY.md`: Long-term global knowledge store.
- **Local Honcho**: Local instances (`http://localhost:8000`) activate keyless; Hermes automatically injects a `"local"` placeholder key.
- **Custom Plugins & Memory**: In-tree PRs to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Create external memory plugins implementing `MemoryProvider` ABC (`sync_turn`, `prefetch`, `shutdown`, `post_setup`) or tool plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable via `hermes plugins enable <name>`.
- **Context Compaction**: `ContextCompressor` / `ContextEngine` (`context.engine` in config) automatically prunes old tool results while preserving token budget.

---

### 5. Execution, Autonomy & Observability
- **Tool Limits & Autonomous Loops**: `agent.max_turns` defaults to 90 (override per turn with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). On exhaustion, Hermes asks for a tool-free summary. For long autonomous tasks, run `/goal <task>` (Ralph loop), which persists across turns and resumes with `/goal resume`.
- **Session Interruption & Restarts**: Crashed or restarted sessions are tagged `resume_pending`. Run `/resume` to restore conversation history. Auto-reset defaults to `mode: none`.
- **Skill Usage & Tracing**: Check skill usage metrics via `hermes insights` or `/insights` (stored in `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`). Enable full call-chain tracing via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Security Vulnerabilities**: Report security issues confidentially via GitHub Security Advisories or email `security@nousresearch.com`.
